title: All shop supplies, including a hand-typed amount, go to the Labor row
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • {Location-A}'s Shop Supplies Charge is 10% of labor, and nothing else is invoiced at {Location-A} today.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} is open and not invoiced; it has one labor line of 2.00 hours at $100.00 an hour and one part sold at $50.00; Labor reads {Sales-rep-A} and Parts reads {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-40001.
  • Starting screen: {Work-order-1} is open in a desktop browser at least 1024 px wide.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. On the work order's Finance tab, type a shop supplies amount of $15.00 by hand in place of the calculated $20.00.
  2. Invoice {Work-order-1}.
  3. Open Reports > Sales By Representative, set the date range to today, turn Show Unassigned on and turn the Sales Type column on in the column selector.
  4. Read the Shop Supplies column on both rows for the invoice.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the work order shows Shop Supplies $15.00.
  • Step 2: the invoice is created.
  • Step 3: {Sales-rep-A} has a "Labor" row and {Sales-rep-B} a "Parts" row for the invoice.
  • Step 4: the Labor row shows Shop Supplies $15.00; the Parts row shows a dash.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 10 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 20 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R4: “A Labor row is credited with Labor Invoiced, Labor Margin, labor-line fees and discounts, Hrs Worked, Hrs Invoiced, Labor Delta and all of the invoice's Shop Supplies, including an amount typed by hand.”
  • S5-R15: “On a Labor row the parts columns show a dash, and on a Parts row the labor, hours and Shop Supplies columns show a dash, not $0.00. $0.00 is shown only for a real zero. A row that holds both sides, one person on both, keeps the report's rule that an invoice with no labor shows Labor Delta 0.0.”
  • Key Decisions, shop supplies: “Shop supplies go to the Labor side. ShopView calculates shop supplies from the labor total, so the whole charge, including an amount typed by hand, is credited to Labor. Whole-invoice fees and discounts are shared by the size of each side. Fees and discounts on a part line or a labor line already belong to that side.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
